newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican guerrilla says he was tortured by army.
newsitem.headline: Mexican guerrilla says he was tortured by army.

text.p: A Mexican leftist guerrilla claimed on a videotape released on Friday that he was captured by the Mexican army, held for four months and was savagely tortured before escaping to rejoin his comrades.

The rebel known as Commander Rafael made his claims before a small group of journalists at a clandestine site in Mexico City on Thursday. A videotape of the news conference was made available to Reuters on Friday.

Rafael is a member of the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), a leftist armed movement that unveiled itself last year and briefly launched a series of bloody attacks on military installations. The group says it has taken up arms to combat a corrupt and anti-democratic government that has sacrificed the needs of the poor while courting international investors.
The EPR has been inactive militarily in recent months, concentrating on a propaganda campaign that included the session with Rafael.
Blindfolded reporters were taken to a safehouse where the walls, ceilings and floors were lined with brown craft paper.

Rafael, a woman believed to be his wife and two rebel commanders sat a table, flanked by three armed guards with AK-47 assault rifles. All wore neatly pressed green military uniforms with the EPR symbol on one shoulder, matching baseball caps and bandanas covering their faces.

"Perhaps after this nothing is the same," Rafael said in a slow, monotone account that lasted nearly two hours. "The after-effects of the torture remain, and they are considerable. But my conviction, my decision for the struggle, that can never ... it is a commitment."
Rafael said he was captured in October while arranging a secret meeting between guerrillas and reporters and was taken to two "torture centers" in Guerrero state and Mexico state.

He said he was subjected to all manner of torture, including being stripped naked and having electric shocks administered all over his wet body. Rafael said his interrogators wanted to know where his comrades were hiding and where the EPR planned to attack. He said he escaped when soldiers were called away from his room.
The Mexican army's public relations office said the army would not be able to respond to the allegations on Friday.
